label: trullate
reason: Matches standard usage (trowel-shaped, broadest below the middle, lower sides shorter). 2-D shape is the right parent: PATO rhomboid (PATO:0001938) is defined as an oval, spheroid shape, and a trullate outline is not a parallelogram. Its mirror term obtrullate should sit under the same parent.

label: complanate-foliate
definition: A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's leaves spreading in one plane, so that the leafy shoot appears flattened.
reason: The synonym does not fit: in most floras 'complanate' on its own means flattened (complanate stems, petioles, seeds), which is PATO flattened (PATO:0002254), so as an exact synonym it would send those statements to this class. Keep 'complanate' only as a related synonym, or match it to this class only when the leaves or the leafy shoot are the subject. Leaf is not a proper bearer; the shoot is.

label: helicoid
reason: Correct for a helicoid cyme (bostryx): successive branches on the same side, so the sympodium curves in a helix; bostrychoid is a true synonym. The coiled parent matches the sibling scorpioid (FLOPO:0991179).

label: catadromous
reason: Matches fern usage: the first segment or vein of each division is basiscopic. The opposite is anadromous. Position is a suitable parent.

label: sour
reason: The class and definition are right, and PATO has bitter (under flavourful) but no sour. The synonyms do not fit as exact: 'acid' clashes with PATO acidic (PATO:0001429, a pH quality), and 'acidulous'/'acidulé' mean slightly sour. Make acidulous, acidulé and acid related synonyms; keep tart as exact.

label: interpetiolar
reason: Standard usage (e.g. Rubiaceae stipules), well formed. It is the counterpart of intrapetiolar (FLOPO:0991290).

label: gynodioecious
reason: Correct: female plants and bisexual (hermaphrodite) plants in the same species. Matches the phenotypic sex siblings (dioecious, andromonoecious). Flower is not a proper bearer; the plant is.

label: monolete
reason: The definition is correct, but the parent is inconsistent with its sister term trilete (FLOPO:0991308), which is under shape (PATO:0000052). Monolete and trilete describe the same feature (the form of the laesura), so they need one parent. Either move monolete to shape, or move both to structure.

label: acrostichoid
reason: Correct: sporangia spread over the whole lower surface of the fertile lamina, not in discrete sori (as in Acrostichum). Spatial pattern is a good parent.

label: ancipitous
reason: Standard: flattened, with two sharp or narrowly winged edges (two-edged). Flattened is the right parent.

label: callus-tipped
reason: Correct and well formed; callous-pointed is a true synonym.

label: sympodial
reason: Correct description of sympodial growth (each lateral takes over when the apex before it stops growing). Branched is an acceptable parent; it is the counterpart of monopodial.

label: starchy
reason: Correct; amylaceous is the glossary synonym. Composition is the right parent. PATO has no such term.

label: semicordate
reason: PATO heart shaped allows 'a sinus or rounded lobe at the base', so a base that is cordate on one side only fits under it. The definition matches the glossary (half-cordate, a basal lobe on one side).

label: tetradynamous
reason: Correct (Brassicaceae: six stamens, four long and two short), and the definition rightly names the androecium as the bearer. Annotations are to 'stamen', so the mining should map them to the androecium.

label: palmatifid
reason: Correct (palmately cut about halfway to the base) and consistent with pinnatifid under pinnately lobed.

label: semisagittate
reason: Correct and well formed; it parallels the other half-shapes.

label: obtrullate
definition: A 2-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's outline being shaped like an inverted trowel: angular at base, sides and apex, broadest above the middle, with the two upper sides shorter than the two lower sides.
reason: Wrong parent. PATO rhomboid (PATO:0001938) is defined as 'a spheroid quality ... oval and a little angular in the middle', which does not describe a trowel outline, and its mirror term trullate (FLOPO:0991336) is under 2-D shape. Move it to 2-D shape, with a definition written to mirror trullate's.

label: extrastaminal
reason: Correct: a disc or nectary outside the stamens. Position is a good parent.

label: monopodial
reason: Correct and the counterpart of sympodial.

label: obreniform
reason: Correct (kidney-shaped, attached at the rounded side, notch at the far end). PATO reniform does not fix where the notch is, so it can be the parent. Note that obcordate was placed under 2-D shape instead; aligning the two would be cleaner.

label: extravaginal
reason: Correct grass and sedge usage (innovations break through the base of the sheath); it is the counterpart of intravaginal.

label: vesicular
reason: Two meanings in one class: 'vesiculose'/'vesiculate' mean covered with small bladder-like vesicles (a texture), but 'vesicular' in floras is mostly used of calyces and fruits to mean bladdery or inflated, a shape (PATO inflated). The calyx and fruit bearers suggest the second sense. Either limit the class to the surface sense (label vesiculose, with vesicular as a related synonym) or file 'vesicular calyx/fruit' under inflated.

label: stolon-like
reason: Follows the existing '-like' resemblance pattern under shape and the meaning is right. Its horizontal growth is also about orientation, and the tuber and root bearers are doubtful, but the class is usable.

label: saprophytic
definition: A trophic quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its lacking or nearly lacking chlorophyll and obtaining its carbon and nutrients from soil fungi associated with its roots, which in turn take them from dead organic matter or from other plants.
reason: Flowering plants called 'saprophytes' in floras are mycoheterotrophs: they do not take up dead organic matter themselves. The current text mixes the two ideas. Holomycotrophic (FLOPO:0991374) overlaps and should become a subclass of this class.
